text: Show by reduction that "does this program ever print hello?" is undecidable. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: // Suppose printsHello(Q) is decidable. Given any P and x, build Q as:
// Then Q prints hello exactly when ___ .
// So deciding printsHello would decide halting -- which is impossible.
answer: run P on x|System.out.println("hello")|P halts on x
explanation: That technique is reduction, and it is how undecidability spreads without a new diagonal argument each time. By the same route: does this program reach line 42, do these two programs compute the same function, does this program dereference null, does it contain a virus. Rice's theorem generalises all of it — every non-trivial property of a program's *behaviour* is undecidable.
